issues.location: Inf(X) displayed formula and its closing delimiters
issues.finding: The frozen formula requires a globally injective function and an element of X missing from its image of X, but does not require u[X] to lie in X. A finite proper subset can therefore satisfy it. The frozen display also has a mismatched closing parenthesis/bracket suffix.
issues.proposed_resolution: Require X(x) implies X(u(x)) before the global-injection condition and balance the final quantifier/parenthesis delimiters. With the image contained in X, the display expresses Dedekind infinitude of X under the ambient cardinality assumptions.

issues.finding: The frozen formula requires X(z), excluding the empty enumerable subset. Its universal clause ends X=Y; taking Y as the full domain satisfies that clause's antecedent, forcing X to be the whole domain even when a proper subset is enumerable.
issues.proposed_resolution: Add an empty-X disjunct and replace X=Y by X subseteq Y in the minimal-orbit clause. The closure of X then gives the other inclusion for nonempty X.

issues.finding: The frozen condition says every subset of X is finite or of size aleph-zero while X itself is not of size aleph-zero. Because X is a subset of itself, no uncountable X satisfies this; finite X can satisfy the displayed formula.
issues.proposed_resolution: Require X to be nonenumerable and every nonenumerable subset Y of X to be equinumerous with X. This expresses the least uncountable cardinality under the usual choice-based cardinal comparison, with a corrected explanatory sentence.
